description: Collection of assets that work together as a system to contain, collect, transport, treat, and safely dispose of or reuse wastewater and faecal sludge
Functional or administrative subdivision of a larger sanitation system

Physical location where specific functions are performed in the collection, transport, treatment, disposal, or reuse of wastewater and faecal sludge; optional, used to organize or locate the assets contained in large and complex systems.
Location or facility where users access sanitation services, including toilets, latrines, urinals, and communal or public sanitation blocks
Property or customer location that receives sanitation service
Structure that holds excreta and wastewater at or near where they are generated; some types also provide partial treatment
Mobile asset used to empty, transport, or transfer faecal sludge, septage, or wastewater
Structure that provides access to a sewer for inspection, cleaning, and maintenance; includes inspection chambers and cleanouts
Section of a piped network that joins two or more pipes or conduits
Mechanical device designed to close off or regulate the flow of wastewater, sludge, air, or other fluids in a pipe or closed conduit
Structure or device that diverts, splits, restricts, releases, or measures flow in an open channel or basin
Anything that is constructed or built with a fixed location on the ground
Device that supplies electrical power for use by electrical equipment, such as a generator, solar power system, wind turbine, or connection to a power grid
Electrical or electronic device
Device for measuring the flow rate of wastewater, effluent, or sludge through a pipe or open channel
Location or access point that allows a sample of influent, effluent, sludge, or receiving water to be collected for testing
Device that measures a physical condition or parameter of interest
Device that conducts periodic or continuous measurements of a wastewater, effluent, or process quality parameter
Device that automatically records measurements over time from connected sensors, meters, or analyzers, and stores the data locally or transmits it to a remote system
Mechanical or electromechanical device that increases the hydraulic head (pressure) of a fluid flowing through it

Structure or container used to hold wastewater, sludge, chemicals, or other fluids within a conveyance network or treatment facility; on-site vessels such as septic tanks are classified under Containment
Equipment or process unit that improves the physical, chemical, or biological quality of wastewater or faecal sludge, including separation, stabilization, and dewatering of solids
Structure that discharges treated or partially treated effluent to the soil for infiltration and/or evapotranspiration
Point or structure where effluent, overflow, or emergency discharge leaves the system and enters a receiving water body or the environment
Any other type of vertical asset not defined elsewhere in this standard
Conduit that carries wastewater, sludge, or other fluids from one location to another

Artificial open or covered channel constructed to convey wastewater, effluent, or combined flows from one location to another. Includes natural watercourses that have been substantially modified (lined, regraded, or walled) and are managed as part of the system
